TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Banda Sea, southern approaches
DATE 25 November 2028 · 0540 local
SIDE Royal Australian Navy
WINDOW 75 min, closes at 112
J-15 carrier fighter. Photo supplied by the SEST author
"Under pressure, you don't rise to the occasion - you sink to the level of your training."
- military training maxim, speaker unknown; often called a SEAL saying

BANDA SEA, before dawn. HMAS STUART, an Anzac-class frigate, took a hit forward on the twenty-third screening Ford's oiler group north of here, outside your part of the fleet action. She has one shaft, six knots, and thirty-one wounded who need a hospital that is a day and a half away at the speed she can make.

Ford's group went north-west without her. A Kilo has been working the southern approaches since the fleet action, and the enclave still has a strike pair that comes south to look. The ceasefire is two days off and nobody has told either of them.

Bring her south-south-east to the line where the tug from Darwin meets her. The Chief Engineer requests six knots to protect the damaged shaft. Match the escort plan to that speed and keep the route ahead clear.
Commodore Alex Mercer
COMMANDER'S INTENT
One shaft, six knots, thirty-one wounded. Bring STUART to the line before somebody with a torpedo finds her, and do not drive her faster than the Chief says she will go.
• Bring STUART to the line
• Harm no neutral shipping
Your detachment. HMAS Stuart, one shaft. Two neutral merchants on the same approach. Opposing: one Kilo, one J-15D pair.

The planned window is 75 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 37 minutes more; the operation is closed at 112 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
